# technitium_permissions (Resource)

Manages who may view, modify and delete in one section of the server. The resource owns the section's full lists: users and groups left out lose their rights, except the built-in admin groups, which the server always keeps. List those too, as the server has them, or they show as a change on every plan. Destroying the resource leaves the permissions as they are.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "technitium_permissions" "zones" {
  section = "Zones"

  group_permissions = [
    # The server always keeps the built-in admin groups, so list them as it has them.
    { name = "Administrators", can_view = true, can_modify = true, can_delete = true },
    { name = "DNS Administrators", can_view = true, can_modify = true, can_delete = true },
    { name = technitium_group.ops.name, can_view = true, can_modify = true, can_delete = false },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `section` (String) The section: `Dashboard`, `Zones`, `Cache`, `Allowed`, `Blocked`, `Apps`, `DnsClient`, `Settings`, `DhcpServer`, `Administration` or `Logs`.

### Optional

- `group_permissions` (Attributes Set) The rights of groups, including the built-in admin groups the server keeps. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--group_permissions))
- `user_permissions` (Attributes Set) The rights of individual users. An empty set removes them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--user_permissions))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The resource identifier.

<a id="nestedatt--group_permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `group_permissions`

Required:

- `can_delete` (Boolean) May delete in the section.
- `can_modify` (Boolean) May change the section.
- `can_view` (Boolean) May view the section.
- `name` (String) The group name.


<a id="nestedatt--user_permissions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `user_permissions`

Required:

- `can_delete` (Boolean) May delete in the section.
- `can_modify` (Boolean) May change the section.
- `can_view` (Boolean) May view the section.
- `username` (String) The username.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import technitium_permissions.zones Zones
```
